hypotheses.title: Options 30-Day Variance Risk Premium Rolling Percentile Harvest
hypotheses.economic_rationale: implied_volatility_mean_30 - historical_volatility_30 (option8, 98% coverage) measures the 30-day Variance Risk Premium (VRP). Institutional investors structurally overpay for short-dated put option protection, keeping implied volatility higher than realized historical volatility. Evaluating when this volatility spread reaches a 60-day historical high for each individual equity (ts_rank(..., 60)) and smoothing over 5 days captures persistent options mispricing without lookahead bias. Bounded subindustry ranking prevents instrument weight concentration and ensures zero correlation with price/volume or analyst models, targeting Fitness > 0.50.
confounders: Unanticipated corporate earnings surprises that cause realized volatility to spike violently above pre-announcement implied volatility
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if variance risk premium rolling percentile yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 5-day linear decay of 60-day rolling time-series rank of 30-day Variance Risk Premium.

hypotheses.title: Options Put-Call Open Interest Sentiment De-escalation Momentum
hypotheses.economic_rationale: -pcr_oi_30 (option9, 98% coverage) captures inverted put-call open interest ratio. When put open interest drops relative to call open interest, institutional hedging demand abates and risk tolerance expands. Taking a 60-day rolling time-series rank (ts_rank(-pcr_oi_30, 60)) benchmarks each firm against its own historical options distribution, isolating genuine positioning sentiment breakouts. A 5-day linear decay and subindustry neutralization eliminates noise while guaranteeing weight is perfectly distributed across TOP3000.
confounders: Broad market index hedging using equity option collars that temporarily skews single-stock put-call ratios
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if put-call open interest sentiment momentum yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 5-day linear decay of 60-day rolling time-series rank of inverted 30-day put-call open interest ratio.

hypotheses.title: Pure Supply-Chain Competitor Return Lead-Lag Momentum
hypotheses.economic_rationale: In corporate supply-chain and competitor networks (pv13), direct competitors (rel_ret_comp, 82% coverage) share macroeconomic factor exposure, supplier bases, and end-market demand. Due to fragmented order flow, competitor stock returns systematically lead focal equities. Evaluating direct competitor returns relative to their 60-day rolling distribution (ts_rank(rel_ret_comp, 60)) captures pure industry revaluation waves without using close or vwap. A 5-day decay and subindustry ranking ensures bounded weights and zero self-correlation.
confounders: Firms undergoing structural distress whose competitors gain market share at the focal firm's direct expense
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if pure competitor lead-lag yields Sharpe < 1.25 or Fitness < 0.50 in TOP3000.

candidates.rationale: Subindustry-neutralized 5-day linear decay of 60-day rolling time-series rank of direct competitor return.
